outputs.name: Fusion partners along the fused transcript

renders._yaml:
- component: advanced_viz
  id: fusion_exon_layout
  title: Exons kept in each fusion
  description: |-
    Each fusion is drawn as two partner lanes in exon units: the exons the fused transcript keeps and the exons it loses are drawn as separate blocks, and the breakpoint sits between the two partners. The colour is the phasing of the fusion. It answers which exons each partner contributes to a fusion.
    How to read: a fusion keeps the 5' partner's exons up to its last fused exon and the 3' partner's exons from its first fused exon on, the FusedExonUp and FusedExonDown LINX reports. Many lost exons on the 3' partner mean a large part of its protein is missing.
    Note: LINX publishes no residue coordinates per fusion, so the axis is the exon rank and not the amino-acid position.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hartwigmedical/hmftools/master/linx/README.md
  kind: fusion_structure
  roles:
    fusion_id: fusion
    partner: partner
    feature: feature
    start: start
    end: end
    breakpoint: breakpoint
    retained: retained
    colour_by: phased

- component: table
  title: Fusion exons table
  description: |-
    Each row is a block of exons of one partner of a fusion, kept or lost, with its start and end in exon units. It answers exactly which exons are retained.
    How to read: filter on a fusion to read its two partners side by side.

- component: card
  id: fusion_count
  title: Predicted fusions
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of distinct gene pairs LINX predicts to be fused, and the bars rank the phasing outcomes. It answers how many fusions there are and whether they keep the reading frame.
    How to read: LINX sets phased when a fusion can be formed after allowing for exon skipping, so in-frame and skipped-exon fusions can make a protein. Out-of-frame fusions usually do not.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hartwigmedical/hmftools/master/linx/README.md
  column: fusion
  aggregation: nunique
  aggregations:
  - count
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: phased
  top_n_count: 3
  caption: fusions, by phasing
  headline: true

- component: figure
  id: fusion_phase_bar
  title: Fusions by phasing and reported type
  description: |-
    Each bar counts fusions by phasing and each segment splits them by the reported type, the class of known or promiscuous pair LINX matched. It answers which kinds of fusion are in frame.
    How to read: a reported type of NONE means no match to the known fusion knowledgebase. Known pairs that are in frame are the highest-confidence calls, so open them first in the table.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hartwigmedical/hmftools/master/linx/README.md
  visu_type: bar
  dict_kwargs:
    x: phased
    color: reported_type
    labels:
      phased: Phasing
      reported_type: Reported type
      count: Fusions

- component: advanced_viz
  id: fusion_record
  title: Fusion record
  description: |-
    One fusion shown as labelled fields: its partners, transcripts, region types, phasing, reportability and the SV chain behind it. It answers what is known about the fusion picked in the table.
    How to read: select a row in the table to fill the card. The reportable reasons field says why LINX did or did not report the fusion.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hartwigmedical/hmftools/master/linx/README.md
  kind: record_card
  roles:
    id: fusion_id
    title: fusion

- component: interactive
  id: fusion_phase_filter
  title: Phasing
  description: |-
    Pick one or more phasing outcomes to keep. It filters every tile of the tab to the fusions with those outcomes.
    How to read: keep INFRAME and SKIPPED_EXONS to see the fusions that can form a protein.
  interactive_type: MultiSelect
  column_name: phased

- component: table
  id: fusion_table
  title: Predicted fusions table
  description: |-
    Each row is a candidate fusion with its partners, phasing, reportability, fused exons and the protein domains kept and lost. It answers which fusions to follow up and lets a row selection fill the record card.
    How to read: sort by reported, then by likelihood, and read the reportable reasons for the ones LINX did not report.
  row_selection_enabled: true
  row_selection_column: fusion_id

- component: advanced_viz
  id: sv_chords
  title: Structural variants across the genome
  description: |-
    Each chord joins the two breakends of a structural variant on a ring of chromosomes. The colour is the event type LINX resolved its cluster to and the width is the junction copy number. It answers where the genome is rearranged and how.
    How to read: many chords between the same two chromosomes suggest a translocation or a complex event. A dense knot on one chromosome is a cluster of local rearrangements.
    Note: a single breakend has no partner locus, so it is not drawn here but it stays in the counts and the table.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hartwigmedical/hmftools/master/linx/README.md
  kind: genome_chord
  roles:
    chrom_a: chrom_a
    pos_a: pos_a
    chrom_b: chrom_b
    pos_b: pos_b
    label: label
    weight: junction_copy_number
    category: resolved_type
    sample: sample

- component: card
  id: sv_count
  title: Structural variants
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of structural variants, and the bars rank the variant types. The secondary number is the count of chromosomes carrying a first breakend. It answers how rearranged the genome is and by what kind of event.
    How to read: a tumor dominated by one type, such as duplications or translocations, points to a particular mutational process. Open the chord view to see where.
  column: chrom_a
  aggregation: count
  aggregations:
  - nunique
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: type
  top_n_count: 3
  caption: SVs, by type
  headline: true

- component: card
  id: sv_cluster_count
  title: Clusters
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of clusters LINX groups the variants into, and the ring splits the variants by the category of their cluster. It answers how many independent events there are and whether they are simple or complex.
    How to read: LINX clusters variants whose breakends are within 5 kb of each other by default, so one complex event can hold many variants. A large share of complex clusters means a heavily rearranged genome.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hartwigmedical/hmftools/master/linx/README.md
  column: cluster_id
  aggregation: nunique
  aggregations:
  - count
  secondary_layout: donut
  breakdown_col: cluster_category
  caption: SVs, by cluster category

- component: card
  id: junction_cn_spread
  title: Junction copy number
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median copy number of the rearranged junctions, and the box shows the quartiles. It answers how many copies of a rearrangement the tumor carries.
    How to read: a higher value means more copies of the rearranged junction in the tumor. Compare variants of the same event type to find the most amplified ones.
  column: junction_copy_number
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: median, with its spread

- component: figure
  id: resolved_type_bar
  title: Variants by resolved event type
  description: |-
    Each bar counts structural variants by the event type LINX resolved their cluster to, and each segment splits them by the raw variant type. It answers what kinds of events the variants form.
    How to read: simple deletions and duplications are single variants. Complex or chained events are the ones that bring several variants together.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hartwigmedical/hmftools/master/linx/README.md
  visu_type: bar
  dict_kwargs:
    x: resolved_type
    color: type
    labels:
      resolved_type: Resolved event type
      type: Variant type
      count: Variants

- component: interactive
  id: sv_type_filter
  title: Resolved event type
  description: |-
    Pick one or more event types to keep. It filters every tile of the tab to the variants in those events.
    How to read: pick one type to see where on the genome it occurs in the chord view.
  interactive_type: MultiSelect
  column_name: resolved_type

- component: table
  id: sv_table
  title: Structural variants table
  description: |-
    Each row is a structural variant with its breakends, event type, cluster, junction copy number and the genes at each end. It answers which variants hit which genes and lets a row selection filter the rest of the dashboard.
    How to read: sort by junction copy number and filter by event type.
  row_selection_enabled: true
  row_selection_column: label
